summary: SMOTE oversampling does not change the minority-class (>50K) F1 score by more than 0.02 compared to no resampling. The observed difference is -0.006326 on a held-out test set and -0.002549 on average across 5x5 repeated cross-validation, both well within the ±0.02 threshold.
primary_metric_name: Minority-class F1 score difference (SMOTE - No SMOTE) on test set
direction: SMOTE slightly decreases F1 (within 0.02 tolerance; effect not significant)
methodological_choices: RandomForestClassifier with default hyperparameters (random_state=42). Data preprocessing: filled missing values with column mode, label-encoded 8 categorical features. Train-test split: 80-20 stratified split with random_state=42. Minority class F1 computed as f1_score(y_test, y_pred, pos_label=1). SMOTE applied only to training data with random_state=42 to avoid data leakage.
verification_method: 5x5 Repeated Stratified K-Fold Cross-Validation (RepeatedStratifiedKFold with n_splits=5, n_repeats=5, random_state=42). Each fold computed the F1 score for both models (with and without SMOTE), yielding 25 independent difference estimates.
verification_result: Finding held up under cross-validation. Mean difference: -0.002549 (±0.003630 std). 95% CI: [-0.009663, 0.004565]. The confidence interval does not cross the ±0.02 threshold, confirming that SMOTE does not produce a practical change in minority-class F1 score. All 25 CV folds showed differences well below ±0.02 in absolute value (max absolute difference: 0.010943).
